correctness.rationale: In the explicitly fixed centrally symmetric six-blocker chamber, q_i are boundary lattice blockers and r_i=q_(i−1)+q_i. Width in primitive integer directions is minimized among (1,0),(0,1),(1,−1) and equals 2+2m, m=min b_i. The chamber has λ1(K)=1 and ε=1/3−m. Neighbor collinearity b_i b_(i+1)=a_i c_(i+1) and central symmetry imply (prod_{0..2} b_i)²=prod_{0..2} a_i c_i. AM–GM forces prod b_i≤1/27. For 0≤ε≤1/90 all b_i=1/3+O(ε), and the exact factorization prod(1−(a_i−c_i)²/(1−b_i)²)=T² gives |a_i−c_i|≤sqrt(27ε), hence each vertex p_i lies within 10sqrt(ε) of the corresponding barycenter of H, proving the Hausdorff estimate. The explicit one-parameter positive-barycentric deformation with a−c=2t and b=(−1+2sqrt(1−3t²))/3 has ε=(2/3)(1−sqrt(1−3t²))~t² and support displacement at u=(−1,−1)/sqrt2 of order |t|, giving sharp exponent. This is chamberwise only.
